I was not able to update my app to Edge Rails because of unresolvable dependencies in gem used in my project. And I was not able to create a new Edge Rails project. Can you provide me any pointers about how to do so ?

All you need to do is generate a new rails project, then change your Gemfile to bundle edge rails:

```
gem "rails", github: "rails/rails"
```

Then `bundle`.

Specifying explicitely set_fixture_class does not help here.

https://github.com/ybart/rails-test-fixtures

@ybart I was able to get your test running with the following two changes:

```
mv test/fixtures/aaa/bbb/greetings.yml test/fixtures/aaa_bbb_greetings.yml
```

and uncomment the line you originally wrote in your test_helper.rb:

```
set_fixture_class :aaa_bbb_greetings => 'Aaa::Bbb::Greetings'
```

Seems to be a possible naming/folder structure error, or should fixtures for namespaced models be able to be in nested folders? @steveklabnik
If this is documented this way I'm okay to give up nested folders.

In Rails 4.0.0 and 4.0.1, if you nest both the `fixtures` and `unit` folders then set this line of code in the test_helper it'll run also. Seems like the more elegant solution but I didn't test on Rails 3.x.

```
# test_helper.rb
# set_fixture_class :aaa_bbb_greetings => 'Aaa::Bbb::Greetings'
set_fixture_class 'aaa/bbb/greetings' => Aaa::Bbb::Greetings
```

```
mkdir -p test/unit/aaa/bbb
mv greetings_test.rb unit/aaa/bbb/greetings_test.rb
```

Edit: fixed the folder structure. I had the unit/fixtures swapped around.
